Chapter 1: Waking Up to a Different Kind of Faith
Most of us grow up with a pretty clear idea of what being religious looks like, don’t we? Maybe it’s repeating the same beliefs in a church pew, following a set list of dos and don’ts, or sticking to a Sunday routine that hardly ever changes the rest of your week.
But every now and then, something happens that flips all those ideas upside down. Sometimes, it's a moment that sneaks up on you—a late-night conversation in a dorm room, a walk through a busy city street, or even a quiet pause of doubt. Suddenly, the old answers just don’t cut it anymore, and you start asking yourself, “Is this really all there is to faith? Could there be more to following Jesus than just believing the right things?”
For one college student, that kind of journey started right in the middle of a restless semester. Picture this: surrounded by classmates racing after grades, internships, and the next big opportunity, he couldn’t shake this growing sense of discomfort. Sure, the lectures and campus ministries felt safe, but something was missing.
It was almost like the stories about Jesus—stories full of healing, compassion, and radical love—were being kept at a distance, locked away in old books and rituals. The gap between what was preached and what was actually lived felt impossible to ignore.
Then, news spread across campus—homeless families had moved into an abandoned church building, seeking shelter. The city wanted them gone, but these families had nowhere else to turn. A small group of students, feeling both curious and uneasy, decided to visit. They figured they’d find chaos and desperation. Instead, they walked into a real community—people sharing food, laughter, and hope, even when everything seemed uncertain.
The students were invited in. Not just to watch, but to listen, to help out, and to see the world through brand new eyes.
That crumbling old church became the place where faith started to come alive—not just as a private belief, but as something you actually live out, even when it gets messy or unpredictable.
The students kept coming back. They learned names, heard stories, and shared meals. And little by little, they realized that the line between “us” and “them” was so much thinner than they’d ever imagined. These families weren’t just recipients of charity—they became teachers, friends, fellow travelers on the journey.
As days passed, the students felt themselves being drawn deeper into the lives of people they’d barely noticed before. They started to see just how easy it is to ignore suffering when it’s out of sight—and how quickly our own comfort can get in the way of real compassion.
That experience left a mark. It made something clear: real faith isn’t about running away from the world’s pain—it’s about stepping right into it, standing alongside those who are hurting, even when it feels uncomfortable.
Of course, waking up like this doesn’t come with a tidy list of answers. In fact, it can open up a whole new set of questions—about money, about security, and about what it actually means to follow Jesus in a world that’s obsessed with success.
But it also sparks a longing for something bigger. Something bold, a bit risky, and rooted in real love. The students began to wonder: What if the teachings of Jesus weren’t just ideals, but actual invitations to live differently? What if ordinary folks could be part of a quiet, world-changing revolution—one small act at a time?
The journey from comfortable belief to radical discipleship rarely happens overnight. It usually starts with a tiny nudge—a moment of discomfort, or maybe just a glimpse of what could be.
For those who are willing to listen, that journey can lead to a life that looks nothing like the one you planned—and everything like the one you truly hoped for.
